extracted.intended_audience: health insurance issuers, State regulators, Exchange administrators, agents/brokers/web-brokers, and stakeholders submitting comments on the HHS Exchange program integrity proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of standards, regulatory requirements, and proposed changes in HHS's proposed rule on the individual market and Exchange program integrity, including issuer premium-payment policies, EHB rules, eligibility definitions, and enforcement/termination standards for agents/brokers/web-brokers. Intended to guide stakeholders who will implement rules or submit comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEP verification and limited pre-enrollment verification (Federal platform)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct SEP verifications and limited pre-enrollment verification for Exchanges on the Federal platform only for consumers who attest to losing minimum essential coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to SEP verifications on Federally facilitated Exchanges; used to limit verifications to attestations of loss of minimum essential coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Enrollment Period length for Medicaid loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Lengthened the SEP from 60 to 90 days for those who lose Medicaid coverage (April 27, 2023 Federal Register; 2024 Payment Notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an administrative change affecting SEP duration for Medicaid losses; included as background precedent for current proposals affecting SEPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment and removal of limitations for monthly SEP (APTC ≤150% FPL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aligned effective dates for coverage after selecting certain SEPs across all Exchanges and removed limitations on the monthly SEP for those eligible for APTC with incomes up to 150 percent of the FPL (April 15, 2024; 2025 Payment Notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precedent describing prior changes to SEP effective dates and monthly SEP eligibility; informs scope of current SEP-related proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: EHB prohibited benefits under §156.115
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on issuers from providing routine non-pediatric dental services, routine non-pediatric eye exam services, long-term/custodial nursing home care benefits, or non-medically necessary orthodontia as essential health benefits (EHB) per §156.115.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists categories excluded from EHB under the EHB Rule (Feb 25, 2013). Note: later payment notices may modify these prohibitions (see separate entry on removal of routine non-pediatric dental prohibition).

rubrics_metrics.name: State selection and notification of EHB-benchmark plan (§156.111 timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: States must notify HHS of the selection of a new EHB-benchmark plan by the first Wednesday in May of the year that is 2 years before the effective date of the new EHB-benchmark plan, otherwise the State's EHB-benchmark plan will default to that State's prior-year EHB-benchmark plan (§156.111 as revised).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory timing requirement for States when selecting a new benchmark; failure to timely notify HHS causes automatic default to prior benchmark for the applicable plan year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of routine non-pediatric dental prohibition as EHB (effective PY2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: Removal of the regulatory prohibition at §156.115(d) on issuers from providing routine non-pediatric dental services as an EHB beginning with plan year 2027 (2025 Payment Notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant change to EHB scope; issuers and States should prepare for dental coverage inclusion starting PY2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actuarially justified plan-specific factors for varying premium rates (§156.80(d)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Require the actuarially justified plan-specific factors by which an issuer may vary premium rates for a particular plan from its market-wide index rate to include the actuarial value (AV) and cost-sharing design of the plan, including, if permitted by State authority, accounting for CSR amounts provided under §156.410, provided the issuer does not otherwise receive reimbursement for such amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which plan characteristics must be included in an issuer's actuarial justification for plan-level rate adjustments; tie to CSR treatment only if State permits and issuer is not reimbursed via other mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming amendment to limited OEP triggering events (§147.104(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removal of §147.104(b)(2)(i)(G), which currently excludes §155.420(d)(16) (the monthly SEP for certain APTC-eligible individuals) as a triggering event for a limited open enrollment period (OEP) for coverage offered outside an Exchange; the intent is not to add §155.420(d)(16) as a triggering event outside Exchanges but to reflect its proposed removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a conforming change to align Part 147 with the proposal to remove the SEP at §155.420(d)(16); HHS requests comment on the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow issuers to attribute initial premium payments to past-due premiums (proposed removal of §147.104(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §147.104(i) that restricted an issuer from attributing payment of premium for new coverage to past-due premiums from prior coverage, thereby allowing issuers (subject to State law) to attribute an enrollee's initial premium payment to outstanding past-due premium amounts and to refuse to effectuate new coverage if that payment does not equal the outstanding debt plus the new monthly premium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal aligns with statutory reading of guaranteed availability and guaranteed renewability; issuers would be required to apply such policies uniformly and consistent with nondiscrimination requirements. HHS seeks comments on this approach and on whether States or Federal rules should set parameters (e.g., time windows, controlled-group scope).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on attribution: person contractually responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal would not permit an issuer to condition effectuation of new coverage on payment of past-due premiums by any individual other than the person contractually responsible for payment of premium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects third parties from being required to pay another person's past-due premiums as a condition of effectuating new coverage. Applies assuming State law does not prohibit the issuer action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform application of premium-payment policy and nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: If an issuer adopts a premium-payment policy that attributes initial premium payments to past-due amounts (including amounts owed to other issuers in the same controlled group), it must apply that policy uniformly to all employers or individuals in similar circumstances in the applicable market and be consistent with applicable nondiscrimination requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors Market Stabilization Rule requirements; uniformity is required to avoid discriminatory application tied to health status. HHS solicits comment on whether to codify specific parameters or leave to States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled-group and temporal parameters for attributing past-due premiums
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Market Stabilization Rule, issuers could attribute payments to past-due premiums owed to other issuers in the same controlled group and were limited to attributing payments for coverage within the prior 12 months; in this proposed rule HHS suggests leaving such parameters to States but seeks comment on whether to codify them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes prior Federal parameters (controlled-group scope and 12-month lookback) and invites public input on whether to maintain, modify, or delegate these limits to States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement when adopting premium-attribution policy (Market Stabilization Rule precedent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuers that adopted the premium-attribution policy (and any issuers in an adopting issuer's controlled group) were required to provide notice of the consequences of non-payment on future enrollment in enrollment application materials and in any notice regarding non-payment of premiums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS notes these are reasonable parameters but believes States may be better suited to set and oversee them; seeks comment on whether to require issuers to establish such terms and on implementation costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement for commenters to provide supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the proposed rule HHS encourages commenters to include supporting facts, research, evidence, and citations (including active hyperlinks) and to upload relevant unpublished materials (data collection instruments, datasets, detailed findings) as part of their comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for effective notice-and-comment submissions: providing citations and documentation assists HHS in analyzing comments; commenters should attach supporting materials where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and treatment of 'lawfully present' for DACA recipients (eligibility for QHP/PTC/APTC/CSRs/BHP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to realign the definition of 'lawfully present' to exclude Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) recipients for purposes of determining eligibility to enroll in a QHP through an Exchange, eligibility for PTC, APTC, CSRs, and enrollment in a BHP in States that elect to operate a BHP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains statutory and policy rationale for excluding DACA recipients (reliance on ACA statutory language, historical HHS interpretation, differences between DHS and HHS statutory authorities); requests comments on this change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination-for-cause standard: 'preponderance of the evidence' (§155.220(g)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to add text to §155.220(g)(2) to state that HHS would apply a 'preponderance of the evidence' standard of proof with respect to issues of fact when assessing potential noncompliance under §155.220(g)(1) to determine whether there was a specific finding or pattern of noncompliance sufficiently severe to terminate an agent's/broker's/web-broker's Exchange agreements for cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS proposes to define 'preponderance of the evidence' at §155.20 as proof by evidence that, compared with evidence opposing it, leads to the conclusion that the fact is more likely true than not. Rationale: typical Federal civil/admin standard; HHS considered alternatives (clear-and-convincing, beyond-a-reasonable-doubt) and the severity of potential consequences. HHS seeks comment on whether a different standard would be more appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange-agreement specificity on impermissible conduct and consumer consent documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to provide greater specificity and precision in Exchange agreements for PY2026 and beyond regarding impermissible conduct by agents, brokers, and web-brokers and to address requirements ensuring they have obtained and documented receipt of consumer consent to collect personally identifiable information (PII) and help consumers apply for and/or enroll in QHP coverage offered through the FFE or SBE-FP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim is increased transparency and clearer guidance to agents/brokers/web-brokers about prohibited conduct and documentary proof of consumer consent; HHS seeks input on actions or subject matters that should be specifically outlined in Exchange agreements.
